title: Give the goal that counts Daniel's queue a place on the dashboard so it is read every evening
ask: hq/data/goals/executive.json is read by nothing because the dashboard iterates hq/data/pillars.json. Give it a home: either an executive pillar row on the dashboard side panel that renders the goal's reading (queue_state / waiting_on_you, target 0, and oldest_waiting_days), or the goal on the reader's band itself. Record the reading nightly to hq/data/history so the burn-down is a fact, not a memory. Every sentence per docs/WRITING.md.
first_action: Read load_goals and the dashboard's pillar loop in hq/server.py and hq/static/app.js; pick the smaller of the two homes and wire it.
source_message: Daniel said yes to the arrival rule (S-16) and the spawn rule (S-17) on 2026-09-20; docs/QUEUE_TO_ZERO.md §12 is the build order.

result:
The work is done and verified in the worktree. Here is what Daniel reads.

Your queue goal now has a home and a record. The dashboard's side panel opens with a row called "What waits on you", above the pillars and never folded away. It shows the count, what the count is made of, how long the oldest item has waited, and the goal itself. Tonight it reads 51 waiting on you: 49 finished pieces of work and 2 decisions, the oldest 16 days. Clicking it goes to the work page.

Every evening at nine, HQ writes one line to its history folder with that night's count, its split, the oldest age and the target. One line per day, never two. The row reports the change since the first recorded night, so the burn-down becomes a fact on disk rather than something we remember. Because the file is written by the running HQ process, the first line lands the first evening HQ runs this code, which means HQ needs a restart after this lands. Until then the row says no night is on file yet.

Three things worth knowing:

- **The number was two numbers.** The old side-panel line and the goal counted decision cards by different rules, so they could disagree. Both now read one shared count, and the nightly record reads the same one.
- **The age reading was blind to decision cards.** It only aged finished work, so with two decisions open and no work it said nothing was waiting. It now ages decision cards from the day the card was filed.
- **I chose the side panel over an executive pillar.** A pillar drags in a detail page, a commit feed and a lead, none of which the goal needs. The goal also stays out of "the one thing" at the top of the page: it will be red every day until the queue is empty, and the count is already on the panel beside it.

The new text passes the writing check. The check does flag one older phrase on the Q-111 decision card that predates this work and is already filed as work, not a failure. The hourly goal journal now records this goal's state alongside the pillar goals, so its "failing since" date will be known too. A test pins the one-line-per-night rule and runs in CI.
